home.title: How much sun does this spot get?
home.lede: Every seed packet and plant label is written in hours of direct sun. Almost nobody knows what their own garden, balcony or roof actually gets.
home.body:
Sunplot answers it with a number. Not where the sun is — that is the easy half — but how much of it reaches this spot, once the fence, the garage and next door's lime tree have taken their share.

Point the camera at the skyline and sweep a finger along the tops of the roofs and trees. Sunplot walks the day a minute at a time and counts only the light that gets through.

What it tells you

  • Hours of direct sun today, graded the way plant labels are: full sun, part sun, part shade, full shade.
  • When the sun arrives and when it leaves, and how the day is broken up.
  • The whole year: when full sun starts and ends, and the weeks that get none at all.

What it does not do

  • No account. There is nothing to sign up for.
  • No servers. Everything is worked out on the phone and works with no signal.
  • No subscription. One payment unlocks the year view and the widget, for good.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: Sunplot has no servers, no accounts and no analytics. Nothing you do in the app is collected, and nothing leaves your device.
privacy.body:
What stays on the device

  • Location. Used to work out where the sun travels overhead, because the answer changes with latitude. It is read on the device and never transmitted.
  • The camera. The live view lets you trace the skyline. No photo or video is recorded, saved or sent.
  • Motion. The compass tells the app which way the phone points, so the sun's path lines up with what the camera sees.
  • Your spots. The places you save and the skylines you trace are stored in the app's own storage on the device.

What is not collected

No identifiers, no usage statistics, no crash reporting, no advertising, no third-party kits of any kind. There is no server to send anything to.

Purchases

The one-time purchase is handled entirely by Apple. Sunplot never sees your payment details, and Apple's own privacy policy covers that transaction.

Children

Sunplot collects nothing from anybody, of any age.

Deleting your data

Deleting the app removes everything it has stored. There is nothing held elsewhere to request or erase.

Changes

If this policy ever changes, the date at the foot of this page changes with it.

support.title: Support
support.lede: Write to {EMAIL}. One person reads it, usually within a day or two.
support.body:
It helps to say which iPhone you have, which version of iOS, and what you were doing when it went wrong. A screenshot is worth a paragraph.

Things worth trying first

The sun's arc does not line up with the sky

That is the compass, not the maths. Wave the phone in a figure of eight, and keep away from speakers, magnets and car dashboards. Sunplot says so on screen when it does not trust its own reading.

It says my skyline is not enough

A single tap is not a skyline. Sweep the finger along the rooftops and turn on the spot as you go; the counter shows how much of the horizon you have covered.

I bought it and it asks me to buy it again

Tap Already bought it? Restore on the purchase screen. Purchases are tied to the Apple Account that made them.

Why does it want my location?

The sun's path depends on latitude far more than people expect. The position is used on the device and goes nowhere.
